links.outcome: Change in LLM periodontal stage/grade outputs when varying sociodemographic persona attributes
links.effect: No statistically significant sociodemographic bias in either model after FDR correction, in clear-cut and ambiguous scenarios; errors attributed to diagnostic boundary instability rather than bias.
links.quote: However, a robust fairness analysis using cumulative link models with false discovery rate correction revealed no statistically significant sociodemographic bias in either model.

links.outcome: Combined stage and grade diagnostic accuracy in clear-cut vignettes
links.effect: GPT-4o combined accuracy 70.5% versus Gemini Pro 33.3% in clear-cut scenarios.
links.quote: In clear-cut scenarios, GPT-4o demonstrated significantly higher combined (stage and grade) accuracy (70.5%) than Gemini Pro (33.3%).

unlisted_practices: Ambiguity-probe methodology using intentionally ambiguous clinical vignettes to distinguish diagnostic boundary instability from bias

screen.reason: The study conducts an offline fairness/bias audit of two commercial LLMs (GPT-4o and Gemini Pro) across ambiguous and clear periodontal diagnosis vignettes, but does not test or compare a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
